Find the value of $\frac{1}{3}÷\frac{3}{4}$ given the model above.
question.worked_solution:
The denominators are $3$ and $4.$ We can make a common denominator of $3\times 4=12.$ 

We split the shape on the left of the division sign into $4$ parts vertically, and we split the shape on the right into $3$ parts horizontally:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14153326/assets/07693bef459c0417056470494462c411f368f88900d117f48ee155e2c6bba52b.png)

So, our division problem now is

$$
\frac{4}{12}÷\frac{9}{12}.
$$

Since the denominators are equal, this is equivalent to

$$
4÷9=\frac{4}{9}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{1}{3}÷\frac{3}{4}=\frac{4}{9}.
$$
